html:
The dumping of toxic waste from the ship Probo Koala, chartered by the oil trader Trafigura, at open sites around Abidjan in August 2006.

A local contractor spread the caustic slops, from cleaning gasoline, at more than a dozen sites. Fumes made the city sick; about 15 people died and tens of thousands sought treatment. The Ivorian government resigned. Trafigura denied fault but paid the Ivorian state about 100 million pounds in 2007 and settled a British lawsuit with victims. A Dutch court fined the company in 2010 over the waste's export. The case became a leading example in the fight against shipping waste to poor countries under the Basel Convention.
sum: The dumping of toxic waste from the ship Probo Koala, chartered by the oil trader Trafigura, at open sites around Abidjan in August 2006.
